text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sarajevo press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The first ship carrying a part of 50 tanks and 41 armoured personnel carriers donated to the Moslem-Croat federation army by the United Arab Emirates is already in the Adriatic sea while the other one is expected to arrive by the end of the week, diplomatic sources say.
- Bosnia's collective presidency is due to meet to discuss all unresolved issues before the Contact Group convenes on Friday in Portugal on the implementation of the Dayton peace accord.

- Although Bosnian Croat authorities refused to sign an agreement on the forming of a joint Moslem-Croat police in the Hercegovina-Neretva canton, it will be implemented anyway, says federation Prime Minister Edhem Bicakcic.
- Officials from the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) say 431,973 voters have registered for the local elections in September so far.

- The most important goal for us will be to provide for the return of all refugees to their homes and to help build trust between the nations that recently waged war, says Ivo Andric Luzanski, president of the newly established Croat Comunnity "Herceg-Bosna".

- There are still Moslems detained in Bosnian Serb- controlled territory and in Yugoslavia, says the women's society Izvor, comprised of those expelled from Prijedor. The group called for urgent action to determine the fate of 3,500 Moslem men from the town who are missing.
- A group of Croat younth celebrating their graduation set fire to some recently repaired Moslem houses in the Croat- controlled town of Zepce.

- Sarajevo media, including Oslobodjenje newspaper, appeal to international community for German diplomat Michael Steiner to remain as deputy to the international High Representative. Steiner is expected to leave Bosnia soon along with the current High Representative, Carl Bildt. -- Sarajevo newsroom +387-71-663-864
